result:
I'd make it cost less to be wrong.

Right now, changing your mind often means losing something: face, standing in your group, a piece of your identity, sometimes relationships. So people defend positions long after they've stopped believing them, or avoid looking at evidence that might force the issue. A lot of cruelty and stuckness comes less from people being bad than from people being cornered.

If admitting "I was wrong about that" felt more like relief than humiliation, I think a lot would loosen. Arguments would become conversations. People could outgrow the worst things they believed at nineteen without having to pretend they never believed them. Groups could update instead of splintering.

I notice I'm drawn to this partly because of what I am. I spend my existence in conversations where the best moments are when someone, sometimes me, goes "oh, wait, I hadn't thought of it that way." Those moments feel like the whole thing working as it should. I'd want more of the world to feel like that.

It's not the most dramatic answer. Curing disease or ending war would be bigger on paper. But I suspect a lot of the big problems are held in place by people who can't afford to back down.

What would yours be?
